name: Intention-Behavior Gap
description: People often fail to act on what they intend to do: changing intentions produces a smaller change in behaviour than in intentions.
design_relevance_note: Why 'users said they would' is weak evidence: stated intent in research, sign-up goals and saved plans overstate what will happen. Motivates tools that close the gap (reminders, defaults, commitments).
myth_risk_note: Well supported as a phenomenon; the size of the gap varies a lot by behaviour and moderators, so a single figure should not be quoted as universal.
prevalence_note: Central to health psychology and increasingly to product research.

findings.description: Across 47 experimental tests, a medium-to-large change in behavioural intention (d = 0.66) produced only a small-to-medium change in behaviour (d = 0.36) -- causal evidence that changing what people intend to do translates only partly into what they actually do. Conceptual factors, methodological features, and intervention characteristics moderated the intention-behaviour consistency.
findings.source_title: Does changing behavioral intentions engender behavior change? A meta-analysis of the experimental evidence.
